packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-10 -- first reader response (unverified image reading)
Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. I opened only PROMPT.md and the packet images (plus my own crops, if any). The only context beyond the images is the batch folder name in the paths given to me.

LAYOUT SURVEY -- FACE 1 (overview image-001.jpg)
Observations:
- Portrait orientation. The object is a composite: a long narrow paper(?) strip on the left (light tan, stained, with several holes) and, overlapping/abutting it on the right, a set of separate pieces of a whiter, parchment-like material: one tall upper piece and below a gap a stack of 5-6 narrow horizontal strips. The pieces are mounted with transparent tape (visible grey strips at the joins).
- The writing runs as single long lines ACROSS the join: each line starts on the left strip and continues onto the right pieces, so the left strip and right pieces seem to be parts of one written sheet (or pieces laid together). I will read lines across the join.
- Script: German cursive (Kurrent-type) in brown ink, roughly 17th-century-looking cursive (observation of letterforms only). Single column, no ruling visible.
- Top of right piece: a word that looks like "Substantia" (or similar) as a heading-like word, set to the right; above it near the top edge a flourish/pen stroke.
- Text is in paragraph blocks, each beginning flush left with a capital (e.g. "Jn ..." lines), with hanging continuation lines. Items include numerals ("3.", "2.", "j.", "36", "39") suggesting a list/inventory of goods with counts (interpretation, tentative).
- A small mark/symbol centred on one of the lower strips (looks like a single letter or paragraph mark).
- Lower left corner: modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Fag. 3k(?)" (archival shelfmark-type note, modern).
- No rubrics, no enlarged decorated initials, no interlinear glosses visible at overview scale.
- Damage: holes and losses on the left strip (dark blotches = holes through to the black background), gaps between right strips, stains.
Tiles image-002 to image-009 are native-resolution tiles of this face (to be confirmed as I view them: expected 2 across x 4 down).

image-002.jpg (tile: top-left of face 1; shows the upper left strip and the left edge of the upper right piece)
Observations: tile shows the left strip from its top edge down to about the 6th text line; the right piece's left edge with a few letters at right. Holes at left margin and middle (tape repairs). Horizontal and vertical fold lines cross the strip. A faint smudged ink shape near top left (offset or erased?), and three small dots at top centre.
Main text (left strip portion only; lines continue on the right piece in image-003):
image-002 l.1 (heading-like line, large initial with flourish above): L(?)r [word: "hat"? / "gant"?] 3. Kirchg(?).  [continues on right]
image-002 l.2: j. lidernes(?) W[hole]d(?) j. Ul[...]  [continues]
image-002 l.3: j. Fürt(?) / Hürt(?) .   par(?) [continues]
image-002 l.4: j. Schürtz(?)/Schürsen(?) j. Th(?)[...]  [continues]
image-002 l.5: Jn Laungen(?) / Jn Lauingen(?) [hole] ... [continues]
image-002 l.6: 5. Ung(?) schaube(?) / schainbe(?)  4.  [continues]
image-002 l.7: (cut at bottom edge; only ascender tops visible)
Right edge of tile (start of right piece): "Sub[...]" (heading word, l. at top), "...Ul", "...run/vun", "...ẞ/ru", "...Ot(?)".
Notes: "j" here is the numeral one (j with dot) as list count. "3." "5." "4." are numerals. Readings of nouns are very uncertain; letterforms are cursive Kurrent with loops.

image-003.jpg (tile: top-right of face 1; shows the upper right piece, overlapping image-002 at its left edge by ~1/10 width)
Observations: whiter material; a strip of old brownish tape at the top edge over a vertical slit/tear; the slit runs down through ~lines 1-3 as a black gap. A pen flourish (two parallel diagonal strokes) at the top left of the piece. Heading word at top left: "Substantia" (initial S with a flourish/"v"-like stroke above it). Large blank space after it at right.
Lines below, numbered from top of this image (each continues the corresponding line of image-002):
image-003 l.1 (heading): Substantia  [S with looped flourish; final -a clear]
image-003 l.2: [Ki]rchg(?). 3. Scapul[slit]r(?) / Scapul[...]. 2. Ca[u/s]ufen(?) / Casulen(?).
image-003 l.3: [...]d j. Ulässlein(?) / Mässlein(?) [nn] [slit] prn(?) Zetz(?) / Zeh(?) . j. J[...]  [the "ü"/two-dot marks over letters visible]
image-003 l.4: [...]rn  wnd(?)ern(?) W[...]d [slit] prn(?) binnen(?) / brunnen(?) Fr(?)[...]
image-003 l.5: j. J[...]  [...]onhoben(?) / hauben(?) .
image-003 l.6: [...]dt(?) 7. Jemand(?) / Pfund(?) n(?). 36. schraiger(?) / Schweiger(?) .
image-003 l.7: [...]be(?)  4. Främbli(?) / Händli(?) [...]chen(?) / -ehen . 2. Frestia(?) / Trestin(?)
Notes: the heading "Substantia" is the most secure reading on this tile. "Kirchg." with abbreviation full stop. Numerals 3., 2., j., 7., 36., 4., 2. secure. Nouns highly uncertain; I give alternatives rather than guess.

Observations: left strip only; at right edge the separated lower strips of the right side appear with small text fragments. Wide blank between l.6 and l.7 here (matches the gap/blank seen in overview, where the right side has a strip with a central mark).

LAYOUT SURVEY -- FACE 2 (overview image-010.jpg)
Observations:
- Portrait. The other side of the composite: now the long tan strip is on the RIGHT (with holes matching face 1's left strip, mirrored) and the whiter pieces on the LEFT: an upper block (itself in two pieces, split vertically near its top) and below a gap a stack of ~6-7 narrow strips. Consistent with this being the reverse face (interpretation).
- Layout: an account/list. Text lines run from the left pieces across onto the right strip; at the far right of the right strip are two narrow ruled money columns, headed at the top "fl." and "kr(?)" (first heading looks like "fl." with a flourish; second faint), with amounts such as "- j. 35", "- 2. 30", "- 2 3 4", "- 4 j", "j 9 40", "- 3 26", "- j 54", "- 40", "- 45", "- 2 5..", "- 24", "- 25", "- 30", "- 2 2j", "- j 30", "- 3", "- j 36", a total-like "66 26", and "35 i0(?)". Vertical ruling lines for the columns are visible.
- Text entries are one or two lines, each ending in a dash leader "--" to the amount.
- A grey rectangle (digital mask / patch over the image) covers the lower part of the right strip; content under it not visible.
- Same brown-ink German cursive as face 1 (observation of letterforms).
- No rubrics, initials, or glosses at overview scale.
Tiles image-011 to image-018 expected 2 across x 4 down.

image-011.jpg (tile: top-left of face 2; upper left block, which is two pieces joined vertically with a black slit between; right edge shows taped join to the right strip)
Observations: line beginnings are cut off at the left edge of the piece (first letters lost), so every line here is incomplete at its start. A blank area of ~5 lines above the first text line. The writing continues to the right strip (image-012).

LIMITATIONS AND SUMMARY
- All 18 images read once each (2 overviews, 16 tiles). I did not reach the image limit; no crops were made (rscratch/packet-10 created but empty).
- Script is a fast, small German cursive; most noun readings are uncertain and given with alternatives. Numerals and the money columns are the most secure content. Latin-looking words on face 1 (Substantia, Mariale, et San[...], Concion[u] Ruraliu D., Procurj, Vdalrici, Libellu de Ju[...]) appear embedded in the German text.
- Line starts on face 2's left pieces are cut off at the left edge of those pieces; face 1 line ends on the right pieces may be similarly truncated at the right edge (the right piece edge is close to the line ends).
- Lower right of face 2 is hidden under a grey digital mask.
- Reading order: on each face I read lines continuously across the joins between the left and right pieces, based on line alignment in the overviews and tiles; that joining is an observation of alignment, not certain.
- Suggested further views: higher-contrast crops of face 1 left strip (faded ink, image-004/006/008) and of face 2 line starts (image-011/013) could improve readings.
- I did nothing beyond the rules. The only potentially identifying text seen was the modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Frg. 9k(?)" on face 1 (image-008), which is a shelfmark-type note, not an identification of the text.
